_note: How each Site CLI command is treated in the documentation, and why.
A Customer Edge runs Linux and a number of third-party daemons. Documenting their
commands would duplicate their own references and imply F5 owns them, so the rule
is: document F5's software, and for everything else document only what is specific
to a CE.
Three tiers, because 'ours' and 'theirs' is not a clean split:
f5-software    F5 wrote it. Full documentation: purpose, syntax, arguments,
captured output, what to look for. Argo, Vega, vpm, vifdump,
configure*, the edit-* set, kubelet params, auxiliary root access.
ce-specific-   A third-party tool, but its output means something particular on a
interpretation CE and getting that wrong misleads. Document the CE-specific reading
and link upstream for the tool's own semantics. FRR does not know
about F5 regional edges; strongSwan does not know which RE a tunnel
terminates on; curl does not know the host and vega namespaces.
passthrough    Plain Linux or third-party, with nothing CE-specific to say. Listed
as available with a pointer to the upstream reference. No prose.
The distinction is not cosmetic: it decides whether a page exists at all, and it
keeps this documentation from rotting into a worse copy of the man pages.

bgp-frr.why: The vrf-id FRR reports is not the vRouter table id that rt --dump takes. Using the BGP number returns 'No such file or directory', which reads as a broken node.

ipsec-strongswan.why: The SA names identify which F5 regional edge each tunnel terminates on, which is the CE-relevant fact and is not something strongSwan documents.

container-runtimes.why: A CE runs both runtimes at once. vpm, argo_watch and site-console are Docker; Kubernetes workloads are CRI-O. A three-entry docker-ps is the complete list, not a symptom.

reachability.why: The two commands run in different network namespaces, so which one fails localises the fault. curl itself has no concept of either.

passthrough._treatment: Listed as available with a pointer upstream. Not documented.

_note: Commands that are NOT on build crt-20250613-3382. Kept because they are real,
but separated so nothing here is mistaken for something a reader can run.
Verified present on build 20260703-e2c462a, which is what the Azure marketplace
image ships as of 2026-07-28. Measured in the Site CLI completion menu over SSH,
on a disposable single-node Azure SMSv2 CE stood up for the purpose (mcn#710):
89 execcli commands there against 82 on crt-20250613-3382, and the difference is
exactly these seven with nothing removed.
These were previously recorded as seen on crt-20260201-0179 via the vpm/debug
catalog on a different tenant. That sighting was never verified here, and it
cannot be reproduced on this site shape: crt-20260201-0179 fails to install on a
single-node Azure SMSv2 CE, at the voucher DaemonSet. So the build named below is
the one they were actually measured on, not the one first reported.
site_state was PROVISIONING at capture, because the node never reached ONLINE.
Presence is still evidence; absence would not have been — and nothing was absent.
_mutating lists three, and collect-database-stats is the one to know about: its
name and the appliance's own description both read as observational, but it runs a
15 second fio RANDOM-WRITE benchmark against the etcd filesystem and lays out a
250 MiB file. It was allow-listed on the strength of the name and run once on the
disposable node; only its own output revealed the writes. A name cannot establish
that a command is read-only, so a test now scans committed captures for write
markers and fails if such a command is on the harness allow-list.
newer_build._verified_how: Site CLI completion menu over SSH; site_state PROVISIONING

_note: collect-debug-info was carried in this file with no provenance. It is in
neither the on-box completion menu nor the debug API catalog. The Site CLI
welcome text does say the CLI 'allows to ... collect debug information for
support', so the name was probably derived from that prose rather than
observed. Deliberately NOT probed: if it exists it collects a support
bundle, and running an unknown command speculatively on a live node is how
a vifdump packet capture got started on a registering CE.
In the vpm/debug catalog but absent from BOTH the on-box completion menu and the
top-level menu, so it is reachable over the API and not from the Site CLI at all.
Deliberately NOT also listed under tiers/passthrough: it was, and that made the
same command both on-box and not-on-box. The reconciliation check now rejects a
command that appears in tiers and in not_on_this_build.

_provenance.method: Site CLI completion menu over SSH, plus the vpm/debug catalog
observations: Enumerated twice, at site_state PROVISIONING and PROVISIONED. Both runs
returned an identical set: 6 top-level and 82 execcli commands. The surface
is therefore not registration-state dependent between those two states, and
an absent command is genuinely absent rather than not yet offered.
